rows.title: Nursing home owner: ‘No one is absconding with any money’
rows.standfirst: Legislators had raised concerns that the owner of Vanderman Place in Willimantic hadn’t distributed raises to workers.

rows.title: Lamont announces $336 million tax cut plan
rows.standfirst: The plan is centered around capping car tax rates and expanding an income tax credit for middle-class property owners.

rows.title: Labor leaders brace to battle Lamont to preserve state workforce
rows.standfirst: With thousands of retirements expected later this year, unions braced Monday for an uphill fight to preserve public services in 2022.

rows.title: Lamont will ask lawmakers to resist the urge to spend big in next CT budget
rows.standfirst: Despite unprecedented surpluses, Gov. Ned Lamont is expected to ask legislators not to spend big in the next state budget.

rows.title: Lamont will finally tap CT’s swelling coffers with new budget
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont will propose budget revisions Wednesday that shift more than $800 million from the state’s coffers into new and expanded programs.

rows.title: Labor: Lamont budget fails to recognize workers who braved the pandemic
rows.standfirst: Essential workers were recognized in Gov. Ned Lamont’s latest state budget, but they would receive much less aid than they sought.

rows.title: Lamont goes big with re-election budget
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont proposed a state budget that funds a middle-class property tax relief program and makes major new investments in many areas.

rows.title: Lamont budget would expand mental health services, other health care initiatives
rows.standfirst: New psychiatric beds and other services for children top a list of mental health investments in the $24.2 billion budget Gov. Ned Lamont unveiled Wednesday.

rows.title: Lamont would remove contracting watchdog’s enforcement powers
rows.standfirst: Contracting watchdog officials say they would lose their power to suspend improper procurements under Gov. Ned Lamont’s budget proposal.

rows.title: House GOP ups the ante in tax-cutting debate
rows.standfirst: House Republicans focus for 2022 is centered on cutting taxes and securing an independent probe of state contracting practices.

rows.title: Budget chief: Lamont doesn’t want to weaken contracting watchdog
rows.standfirst: Melissa McCaw assured state legislators the administration has no plans to strip authority from the state’s contracting watchdog board.

rows.title: Legislators exploring income tax cuts, mansion tax
rows.standfirst: Democratic state lawmakers want to ask more from the rich to ensure new tax relief for CT’s poor and middle-class is sustainable.

rows.title: CT budget panel pushes for tighter control of state contracting
rows.standfirst: The General Assembly’s budget-writing panel is pushing back against Gov. Ned Lamont to assume greater control over contracting policies.

rows.title: Study: Overall CT tax system hits poor, middle class harder
rows.standfirst: People who earned less than $44,758 in 2019 lost nearly 26% of their earnings to taxes, nearly four times the rate paid by CT’s wealthiest.
